accordion-button: The accordion is built on <details>/<summary> now, so the trigger is the summary itself. Put .accordion-header on the <summary> element and drop the nested button.
accordion-collapse: The panel is the <details> element's own content now, revealed by the browser and styled through ::details-content. Nothing wraps the .accordion-body any more.
alert-dark: Removed in v6 with the `dark` theme colour. Rename it to the `-inverse` variant: `inverse` resolves to gray-900 in light mode and gray-100 in dark, so it stands against the page in both schemes instead of staying near-black on a near-black one.
alert-dismissible: The alert lays its children out in a row and pushes a direct-child .btn-close to its end, so the class has nothing left to do. Markup that still carries it renders the same; a close button nested in a wrapper is laid out by that wrapper now, so move it up to be a direct child of the alert.
alert-light: Removed in v6 with the `light` theme colour. Rename it to the `-secondary` variant, which is the light neutral now (gray-100 in light mode, gray-600 in dark). Where the class was painting a plain panel rather than naming a colour, use .bg-4 or .bg-3.
autocomplete-buttons: The adornment buttons are children of the .form-control-group itself now, laid out by the group, so the wrapper is gone. Use .form-control-action / .form-control-cleaner on the buttons.
autocomplete-cleaner: The frame of every field component is the shared .form-control-group primitive now. Use .form-control-action for an adornment button, .form-control-cleaner for the one that clears the value, .form-control-icon for decoration, and .form-control-sm / .form-control-lg on the group for sizing. See the v6 migration guide.
autocomplete-dropdown: The generated options dropdown is the shared combobox surface now (.popup + .combobox-popup), so the component never emits this class - see "Autocomplete and Multi Select share one options menu" in the migration guide. The last selectors carrying it only fed tokens to a teleported dropdown that had stopped existing.
autocomplete-indicator: The frame of every field component is the shared .form-control-group primitive now. Use .form-control-action for an adornment button, .form-control-cleaner for the one that clears the value, .form-control-icon for decoration, and .form-control-sm / .form-control-lg on the group for sizing. See the v6 migration guide.
autocomplete-input: The editable inside a field component is a plain .form-control now — the group strips its frame, so it needs no class of its own. See .form-control-group in the v6 migration guide.
autocomplete-input-group: The frame of every field component is the shared .form-control-group primitive now, so the input group squares off that one class instead of a different wrapper per family. Nothing has emitted these since the primitive landed - the only thing keeping them in the stylesheet was the input-group rules that matched them, which matched no markup.
autocomplete-lg: The frame is the size surface now: put .form-control-sm / .form-control-lg on the .form-control-group. The family-named class declared its tokens on the component root, where the frame's own declarations shadowed them - it never had an effect in v6.
autocomplete-optgroup-label: The generated options dropdown of Autocomplete and Multi Select is one shared surface now — use the unified combobox-* classes (combobox-popup/-header/-all/-options/-option/-optgroup and the selected/indeterminate states).
autocomplete-option: The generated options dropdown of Autocomplete and Multi Select is one shared surface now — use the unified combobox-* classes (combobox-popup/-header/-all/-options/-option/-optgroup and the selected/indeterminate states).

autocomplete-sm: The frame is the size surface now: put .form-control-sm / .form-control-lg on the .form-control-group. The family-named class declared its tokens on the component root, where the frame's own declarations shadowed them - it never had an effect in v6.

callout: Removed in v6 - the base class is padding, margin, a border and a radius, all of which are utilities. Use .p-3 .my-3 .border .rounded together with .border-start-4 and a .border-start-{color} utility for the accent edge.
callout-danger: Removed in v6 with the callout component. The modifier only set the left border colour: use .border-start-danger on the element, alongside .border-start-4 for its width.
callout-dark: Removed in v6 with the callout component and the `dark` theme colour. Use .border-start-inverse alongside .border-start-4 on an element styled with .p-3 .my-3 .border .rounded.
callout-info: Removed in v6 with the callout component. The modifier only set the left border colour: use .border-start-info on the element, alongside .border-start-4 for its width.
callout-light: Removed in v6 with the callout component and the `light` theme colour. Use .border-start-secondary alongside .border-start-4 on an element styled with .p-3 .my-3 .border .rounded.

card-header-pills: Removed in v6. It pulled the pill row out to the card header's padding edge, which suits tabs but not pills - a pill carries its own background, so flush against the header's inner edge it touches the border. Drop the class and keep .nav.nav-pills.
card-link:
Removed in v6. The card body is a flex column now, so two links no longer sit next to each other by virtue of being inline - the class's own inline margin had nothing left to space. Drop it and lay the links out yourself:
OneTwo
.
carousel-dark: Set data-coreui-theme="dark" on the carousel instead. The chrome colours are light-dark() pairs resolved on the element, so the standard theme attribute flips them - and data-coreui-theme="light" pins the white chrome on a dark page the same way.
carousel-item-end: The carousel slides by scrolling now - the browser moves the track, so there is no transform choreography and no in-transition state classes. React to the slide/slid events instead of styling these.
carousel-item-next: The carousel slides by scrolling now - the browser moves the track, so there is no transform choreography and no in-transition state classes. React to the slide/slid events instead of styling these.

chip-dismiss: Renamed to .chip-remove in v6, matching the component's own vocabulary (Chip Input removes a chip, it does not dismiss it). The last selector carrying the old name styled a disabled chip input's remove buttons and matched nothing, so the disabled state never reached them.
chip-light: Removed in v6 with the `light` theme colour. Rename it to the `-secondary` variant, which is the light neutral now (gray-100 in light mode, gray-600 in dark). Where the class was painting a plain panel rather than naming a colour, use .bg-4 or .bg-3.
collapsed: Nothing styles or emits this class any more. The accordion was the only thing that styled it, and its trigger is a <summary> element now, while Collapse marks its triggers with aria-expanded alone. Style a trigger by that attribute: [data-coreui-toggle="collapse"][aria-expanded="false"].

date-picker-cleaner: The v1 picker shells are gone: the pickers are now composed from the section-input field, Calendar and TimeSelection, so the field internals are styled by forms/_form-date-time.scss and the icons are inline SVG rendered by the component. See the v6 migration guide.
date-picker-dropdown: Renamed to .date-picker-popup / .time-picker-popup. The panel is the shared `.popup` surface, and every other family had already dropped the `-dropdown` vocabulary when the options menu became .combobox-popup; the pickers were the last holdout. The class carries the panel's tokens now instead of inheriting them from the field's root, so it works the same teleported, portaled or in place.
date-picker-indicator: The frame of every field component is the shared .form-control-group primitive now. Use .form-control-action for an adornment button, .form-control-cleaner for the one that clears the value, .form-control-icon for decoration, and .form-control-sm / .form-control-lg on the group for sizing. See the v6 migration guide.
date-picker-input: The v1 picker shells are gone: the pickers are now composed from the section-input field, Calendar and TimeSelection, so the field internals are styled by forms/_form-date-time.scss and the icons are inline SVG rendered by the component. See the v6 migration guide.
date-picker-input-group: The frame of every field component is the shared .form-control-group primitive now, so the input group squares off that one class instead of a different wrapper per family. Nothing has emitted these since the primitive landed - the only thing keeping them in the stylesheet was the input-group rules that matched them, which matched no markup.

figure-img: The figure spaces its image and caption with the --cui-figure-gap flex gap now, so the class has no styles left to carry - no bottom margin, no line-height reset. Keep it in your markup or drop it; both render the same.

form-check-reverse: Removed in v6. It right-flushed the label and the control as a pair, which the order utilities express directly, and it was never the settings row (label on the left, control on the right) it is usually reached for - that one is justify-content: space-between. See the v6 migration guide.

link-body-emphasis: The theme classes colour a link now: Reboot resolves a link's colour from --cui-theme-fg, which every .theme-* class sets, so <a class="theme-primary"> replaces <a class="link-primary">. The theme slot is a tone picked for text rather than the raw brand colour - it darkens on a light background and lightens on a dark one, where .link-* gave the same colour in both. Pair it with .link-underline for the underline, which now defaults to currentColor. For .link-body-emphasis use .text-body-emphasis.

modal-backdrop: The backdrop is the native ::backdrop pseudo-element now - no element is inserted into the DOM. Style it through the --cui-modal-backdrop-bg / --cui-modal-backdrop-opacity tokens on .modal.
modal-content: Modal renders on the native <dialog> element now: the positioning shell and the content box are the single <dialog class="modal"> element, so the wrapper layers are gone. Size and fullscreen modifiers sit on the dialog itself. Legacy v5 markup is auto-upgraded at runtime (with a console warning) until v7 - see "Modal and Offcanvas on the native dialog" in the migration guide.

modal-dialog-centered: The browser centers a native modal <dialog> in the viewport, so centering needs no class - it is the default and only behavior.
modal-dialog-scrollable: Renamed to .modal-scrollable, placed on the <dialog class="modal"> itself now that the wrapper layers are gone.
offcanvas-backdrop: The backdrop is the native ::backdrop pseudo-element now - no element is inserted into the DOM. Style it through the --cui-offcanvas-backdrop-bg / --cui-offcanvas-backdrop-opacity tokens on .offcanvas.
pointer-event: Touch is handled natively by the scroll viewport now - drag, swipe and momentum come from the browser, so the touch-action override class has nothing to do.
progress-group: Removed in v6 — a CoreUI-only addition that utilities already cover. It was a flex row with a 100px label column, a header row and a 2px gap between bars. Use .hstack / .vstack with a gap-* utility and put the label column's width in a style; see "Grouping bars" on the Progress page.

progress-thin: Removed in v6 — a CoreUI-only addition that did nothing an inline height does not. Use style="height: 4px" on the .progress, as the Height section shows, or set --cui-progress-height if you also want the stripe geometry to follow.
ratio: The ratio classes set the CSS aspect-ratio property directly now, so the wrapper is gone: put .ratio-16x9 on the element you want sized instead of wrapping it in a bare .ratio. The named classes (.ratio-1x1, .ratio-4x3, .ratio-16x9, .ratio-21x9) keep working. A custom ratio moves from a padding percentage to a real ratio - --cui-aspect-ratio: 50% becomes --cui-ratio: 2 / 1 on .ratio-auto.
showing: Offcanvas state classes are replaced by the native <dialog> [open] attribute; the exit transition still uses .hiding while the JS keeps the dialog in the top layer. There is no entry counterpart to migrate to - [open] is set before the transition starts.
spinner-border-sm: Replaced by .spinner-sm, which works on both spinner types. Spinners are sized in em now, so the small variant no longer has to correct the border width and needed no per-type class. Note that a spinner already takes the font size of whatever contains it, so inside a button or a paragraph you can usually drop the size class entirely.
